recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow **LIQUID Domain** with **Simulation Method = FLIP** as the primary setup, because Blender docs describe FLIP as the splashiest method with dispersed droplets (best match for vigorous wine impact/splash behavior). Keep liquid meshing enabled, tune particle sampling/radius for volume retention and droplet detail, and bake with Cache Type **All** for a single full bake pass.

key_parameters.particle_radius: Increase if liquid appears to disappear/leak numerically; decrease if excess volume appears
key_parameters.sampling: Increase sampling factor to generate more particles/detail
key_parameters.randomness: Lower for cleaner/laminar inflow stream, higher for more turbulent inflow breakup
key_parameters.surface_tension: Increase for stronger cohesion and rounder droplets
key_parameters.high_viscosity_solver: Use only for very thick/slow liquids; not generally required for water-like wine pour

warnings: Disabling the Liquid checkbox removes the attached liquid particle system/settings.
Very high viscosity values are not suitable for making non-fluid/rigid behavior and can cause instability.
Replay cache mode depends on playback sync = Play Every Frame; otherwise prefer Modular or All.
Doc bundle diagnostic warning returned: "No API doc_refs found (expected bpy.types.* or bpy.ops.* references)."
alternative_approaches: Use APIC instead of FLIP if you need a more stable (less chaotic) fill while retaining energetic motion.
Lower FLIP ratio from 1.0 for subtler, smaller-scale splash behavior.
Use Cache Type Modular for stepwise rebakes when iterating mesh/particle stages.
